title.zh: 卷一百九十三 列傳第八十: 忠義一
title.en: Volume 193 Biographies 80: Loyal and Righteous Acts 1
title.raw: 卷一百九十三 列傳第八十: 忠義一 Volume 193 Biographies 80: Loyal and Righteous Acts 1

sentences.zh: 李伯溫，守賢之孫，彀之子也。

translations.literal: Li Bowen was the grandson of Shouxian and the son of Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bowen was a grandson of Shouxian and the son of Gou.

sentences.zh: 長兄惟則，懷遠大將軍、平陽征行萬戶；

translations.literal: His eldest brother was Weize, General of Huaiyuan and commander of ten thousand households on campaign from Pingyang;
translations.idiomatic: His eldest brother Weize held the ranks of General of Huaiyuan and campaign commander of ten thousand households from Pingyang;

sentences.zh: 次伯通。

translations.literal: The next in order was Botong.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Botong.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，錦州張致叛，國王木華黎命擊之，大戰城北，伯通死焉。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year, Zhang Zhi of Jinzhou rebelled; the prince Muqali ordered an attack on him, and in a great battle north of the city Botong died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year Zhang Zhi rebelled at Jinzhou; Prince Muqali ordered him struck down, and in a fierce battle north of the city Botong was killed.

sentences.zh: 伯溫行平陽元帥府事，鎮青龍堡，專任東征。

translations.literal: Bowen acted as head of the Pingyang Marshal's headquarters, garrisoned Qinglong Fort, and was solely charged with the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen ran the Pingyang marshal's office, held Qinglong Fort, and bore sole responsibility for operations in the east.

sentences.zh: 知平陽已陷，弟守忠被執，選驍勇拒守，久之，金人盡銳來攻，守卒夜多遁去，李成開水門導敵入，伯溫登堞樓，謂左右曰：「吾兄弟仗節擁麾，受方面之寄，今不幸失利，當以死報國。

translations.literal: Learning that Pingyang had already fallen and that his younger brother Shouzhong had been captured, he chose the bravest men to hold out in defense; after a long time the Jin brought their full strength to attack, and by night many of the defenders fled; Li Cheng opened the water gate and led the enemy in; Bowen mounted the parapet tower and said to those beside him: "We brothers have borne the commander's staff and banner and received the trust of a whole region; now, having met with misfortune and defeat, we ought to repay the state with our deaths."
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Pingyang had fallen and his brother Shouzhong had been taken, he picked his fiercest troops to hold the fort. After a long siege the Jin threw their full force against it; by night most of the garrison slipped away. Li Cheng opened the water gate and admitted the enemy. Bowen climbed the tower and told his men: "My brothers and I have carried the commander's banner and been entrusted with an entire circuit. Now that we have lost, we must repay the realm with our lives."

sentences.zh: 吾弟已被執，我不可再辱，汝等宜自逃生。

translations.literal: "My younger brother has already been captured; I cannot suffer disgrace again—you should each save yourselves and flee."
translations.idiomatic: "My brother is already a prisoner; I cannot endure another humiliation. You should escape while you can."

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆猶豫不忍去，伯溫即拔劍殺家屬，投井中，以刃植柱，刺心而死。

translations.literal: " The soldiers all hesitated and were unwilling to leave; Bowen at once drew his sword and killed his family members, cast them into a well, planted his blade in a pillar, and stabbed himself through the heart to die.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops hung back, unwilling to go. Bowen drew his sword, killed his household, threw their bodies down a well, set his blade against a pillar, and drove it into his own heart.

sentences.zh: 金人登樓，見伯溫抱柱如生，無不嗟歎。

translations.literal: When the Jin climbed the tower and saw Bowen embracing the pillar as if still alive, none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin soldiers who mounted the tower found Bowen still clasping the pillar as though he lived, and every one of them sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 子守正，自幼時嘗質於木華黎，後為平陽守，活俘虜甚衆，以功授銀青榮祿大夫、河東南路兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: His son Shouzheng had from childhood been held as a hostage with Muqali; later he became defender of Pingyang, took many captives alive, and for his merit was appointed Silver-Green Glory and Blessing Grand Master and marshal of the armies of Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouzheng had been left as a hostage with Muqali in his youth. He later served as defender of Pingyang, took large numbers of prisoners alive, and was made Silver-Green Glory and Blessing Grand Master and marshal of the Hedong South Circuit armies for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 歲庚寅，上黨、晉陽合兵攻汾州，將陷，守正以義赴援，衆寡不敵，別遣老弱百人，曳薪揚塵，多張旗幟，敵懼，遂解去。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year, Shangdang and Jinyang joined forces to attack Fenzhou, which was on the verge of falling; Shouzheng went to its aid out of righteousness, but his numbers were too few to match the enemy; he separately sent out a hundred old and weak men to drag firewood and raise dust, and set up many banners and flags; the enemy grew afraid and thereupon lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year the forces of Shangdang and Jinyang combined to besiege Fenzhou, which was near collapse. Shouzheng marched to its relief on principle, though he was heavily outnumbered. He detached a hundred old men and weak troops to drag brushwood and kick up dust, and spread a great show of banners. The enemy took fright and broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 汾人持牛酒迎犒者，道不絕，且泣謝曰：「幸公完是州，德甚大，願奉是州以從。

translations.literal: The people of Fen came out with oxen and wine to welcome and reward him along the road without cease, and weeping they thanked him, saying: "It is our good fortune that you have preserved this prefecture; your virtue is very great—we wish to offer this prefecture and follow you."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fen lined the road without end, bringing cattle and wine to greet him, weeping as they thanked him: "You have saved our prefecture—your kindness is beyond measure. We would gladly yield this prefecture and follow you."

sentences.zh: 」關中兵屯吉州，酋領楊鐵槍以數千人叛，守正出兵擒之。

translations.literal: " Guanzhong troops were stationed at Jizhou; the chieftain Yang Tieqiang rebelled with several thousand men, and Shouzheng led troops out and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: " Guanzhong troops were encamped at Jizhou when the chieftain Yang Tieqiang rose in rebellion with several thousand men. Shouzheng took the field and seized him.

sentences.zh: 軒成據隰州，守正往擊之，中矢傷足，及歸，瘡甚，會金人完顏合達攻平陽，守正裹瘡戰歿。

translations.literal: Xuan Cheng held Xizhou; Shouzheng went to attack him, was struck by an arrow and wounded in the foot; when he returned the wound was severe; just then the Jin commander Wanyan Heda attacked Pingyang, and Shouzheng, binding his wound, fought and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Cheng held Xizhou, and Shouzheng marched against him but took an arrow in the foot. The wound worsened after he returned. When the Jin general Wanyan Heda assaulted Pingyang, Shouzheng wrapped the injury and fought until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 大帥以其兄守忠代之。

translations.literal: The supreme commander appointed his elder brother Shouzhong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander put his elder brother Shouzhong in his place.

sentences.zh: 守忠官至銀青榮祿大夫、河東南路兵馬都元帥，兼知平陽府事。

translations.literal: Shouzhong rose to the office of Silver-Green Glory and Blessing Grand Master and marshal of the armies of Hedong South Circuit, and concurrently served as administrator of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong rose to Silver-Green Glory and Blessing Grand Master, marshal of the Hedong South Circuit armies, and concurrent prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 壬午冬，平陽公胡景山以青龍堡降。

translations.literal: In the winter of the renwu year, the Duke of Pingyang, Hu Jingshan, surrendered Qinglong Fort.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the renwu year the Duke of Pingyang, Hu Jingshan, surrendered Qinglong Fort.

sentences.zh: 嘗從攻益都，北還，軍將彭智孫，乘間據義州叛，守忠聞之，長驅抵城下，力戰，復之。

translations.literal: He had once followed in the attack on Yidu; on the return north, the army officer Peng Zhisun seized an opportunity to hold Yizhou and rebel; when Shouzhong heard of it he drove at full speed to the foot of the city, fought fiercely, and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: He had taken part in the assault on Yidu. On the march north the officer Peng Zhisun seized a moment of weakness to seize Yizhou and rebel. Shouzhong rode hard to the walls, fought bitterly, and won the city back.

sentences.zh: 丁亥夏四月，金紇石烈真襲擊平陽行營招討使權國王按察兒於洪洞，守忠出援之，會於高梁，師潰入城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the dinghai year, the Jin commander He Shiliezhen launched a surprise attack on the Pingyang campaign pacification commissioner and acting prince Anchai'er at Hongtong; Shouzhong went out to reinforce him; they met at Gaoliang, the army was routed, and they fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the dinghai year the Jin commander He Shiliezhen surprised the Pingyang campaign pacification commissioner and acting prince Anchai'er at Hongtong. Shouzhong marched to his aid; they joined battle at Gaoliang, were routed, and fell back into the city.

sentences.zh: 平陽副帥夾谷常德潛獻東門以納金兵，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The deputy commander of Pingyang, Jiagu Changde, secretly opened the east gate to admit Jin troops, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander of Pingyang, Jiagu Changde, secretly opened the east gate to the Jin, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 金人執守忠至汴，誘以高爵，使降，守忠罵之，語惡，金人怒，置守忠鐵籠中，火炙死。

translations.literal: The Jin seized Shouzhong and took him to Bian; they tempted him with high rank and ordered him to surrender; Shouzhong reviled them with vile words; the Jin grew angry, placed Shouzhong in an iron cage, and roasted him to death over fire.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Shouzhong to Bian, offered him lofty rank, and urged him to submit. He cursed them in the foulest terms. Enraged, they shut him in an iron cage and burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 石珪，泰安新泰人，宋徂徠先生守道之裔孫也，世以讀書力田為業。

translations.literal: Shi Gui was a man of Xintai in Tai'an; he was a descendant of the Song master Shoudao of Culai, and for generations his family had made its living by study and farming.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gui came from Xintai in Tai'an. He was descended from the Song scholar Shoudao of Culai, and his family for generations had lived by the book and the plough.

sentences.zh: 體貌魁偉，膂力過人，倜儻不羈。

translations.literal: His physique was imposing and his strength surpassed other men; he was bold and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and powerfully built, stronger than ordinary men, and free-spirited by nature.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐南渡，兵戈四起，珪率少壯，負險自保，與滕陽陳敬宗聚兵山東，破張都統、李霸王兵於龜蒙山。

translations.literal: When the Jin moved south across the river in the Zhenyou era and warfare broke out everywhere, Gui led the young and strong, relied on dangerous terrain to protect themselves, and with Chen Jingzong of Tengyang gathered troops in Shandong, defeating the armies of Commander Zhang and King Li the Overlord at Guimeng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin court crossed south in the Zhenyou era and war spread on every side, Gui rallied the young men of his district, held the high ground for safety, and joined Chen Jingzong of Tengyang to raise forces in Shandong. At Guimeng Mountain they routed the troops of Commander Zhang and King Li the Overlord.

sentences.zh: 宋將鄭元龍以兵迎敵，珪敗之於亳陽，遂乘勝引兵入盱眙。

translations.literal: The Song general Zheng Yuanlong came with troops to meet the enemy; Gui defeated him at Boyang and thereupon, pressing the victory, led his army into Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Zheng Yuanlong marched out to oppose him. Gui defeated him at Boyang and, riding the momentum, drove his army into Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 會宋賈涉誘殺漣水忠義軍統轄季先，人情不安，衆迎珪為帥，呼為太尉。

translations.literal: It happened that the Song official Jia She lured and killed Ji Xian, commander of the Loyal and Righteous Army of Lianshui, and popular sentiment was unsettled; the multitude welcomed Gui as commander and called him Grand Captain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song minister Jia She treacherously killed Ji Xian, commander of the Lianshui Loyal and Righteous Army, morale collapsed. The troops acclaimed Gui as their leader and addressed him as Grand Captain.

sentences.zh: 歲戊寅，太祖使葛葛不罕與宋議和。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year the Taizu sent Gegebukan to negotiate peace with the Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year Taizu dispatched Gegebukan to treat for peace with the Song.

sentences.zh: 己卯，珪令麾下劉順直抵尋斯干城，入覲，太祖慰勞順，且敕珪曰：「如宋和議不成，吾與爾永結一家，吾必榮汝。

translations.literal: In the jimao year Gui ordered his subordinate Liu Shun to go straight to the city of Xingsigan, enter audience, and the Taizu comforted and rewarded Shun, and moreover charged Gui, saying: "If peace talks with the Song do not succeed, I and you shall be bound as one family forever, and I shall surely honor you."
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year Gui sent his officer Liu Shun to Xingsigan to present himself at court. Taizu received Shun warmly and sent word to Gui: "If the peace talks with the Song fail, you and I shall be one household forever, and I shall honor you richly."

sentences.zh: 」順還告珪，珪心感服，日夜思降。

translations.literal: " When Shun returned and told Gui, Gui's heart was moved to submission, and day and night he thought of surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun returned and reported this to Gui, whose heart was won; day and night he resolved to defect.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，宋果渝盟，珪棄其妻孔氏、子金山，杖劍渡淮，宋將追之曰：「太尉迴，完汝妻子。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year the Song indeed broke the alliance; Gui abandoned his wife, Lady Kong, and his son Jinshan, took sword in hand and crossed the Huai; a Song general pursued him, saying: "Grand Captain, turn back—we will restore your wife and children unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year the Song broke the treaty as expected. Gui left behind his wife Lady Kong and his son Jinshan, sword in hand, and crossed the Huai. A Song officer called after him: "Grand Captain, turn back and your family will be spared."

sentences.zh: 」珪不顧，宋將沉珪妻子於淮。

translations.literal: " Gui paid no heed; the Song general drowned Gui's wife and son in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui would not look back. The Song officer drowned his wife and son in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 遂率順及李溫，因孛里海歸木華黎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Shun and Li Wen and, by way of Bolihai, returned to Muqali.
translations.idiomatic: He then led Shun and Li Wen back to Muqali by way of Bolihai.

sentences.zh: 木華黎悅之，謂曰：「若得東平、南京，授汝判之。」

translations.literal: Muqali was pleased with him and said: "If we take Dongping and Nanjing, I will appoint you to administer them."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali received him gladly and said: "When we take Dongping and Nanjing, I will put you in charge of them."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，木華黎承制授珪光祿大夫、濟兗單三州兵馬都緫管、山東路行元帥，佩金虎符，便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year Muqali, acting by imperial commission, appointed Gui Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, overall commander of the armies of the three prefectures Ji, Yan, and Shan, and campaign marshal of the Shandong Circuit, with a golden tiger tally and discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year Muqali, acting under imperial warrant, made Gui Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, overall commander of the Ji, Yan, and Shan prefectures, and campaign marshal of Shandong, with a golden tiger tally and full discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 後金棄東平，珪與嚴實分據，收輯濟、兗、沂、滕、單諸州。

translations.literal: Later the Jin abandoned Dongping; Gui and Yan Shi divided the territory and gathered in the prefectures Ji, Yan, Yi, Teng, and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin later abandoned Dongping, Gui and Yan Shi divided the ground between them and brought the prefectures Ji, Yan, Yi, Teng, and Shan back under control.

sentences.zh: 癸未，太祖詔曰：「石珪棄妻子，提兵歸順，戰勝攻取，加授金紫光祿大夫、東平兵馬都緫管、山東諸路都元帥，餘如故。」

translations.literal: In the guiwei year the Taizu issued an edict: "Shi Gui abandoned wife and children and led troops in submission; in battle he conquers and in attack he takes—he is further appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, overall commander of the armies of Dongping, and supreme marshal of all circuits of Shandong; the rest of his offices remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year Taizu decreed: "Shi Gui left wife and child, brought his troops over, and wins wherever he fights. He is promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, commander of the Dongping armies, and supreme marshal of all Shandong circuits; his other commissions stand unchanged."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，珪領兵破曹州，與金將鄭從宜連戰數晝夜，糧絕，援兵不至，軍無叛意，珪臨陣馬仆被擒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Gui led troops to storm Caozhou; he fought the Jin general Zheng Congyi for several days and nights in succession; provisions ran out and reinforcements did not arrive; the army showed no sign of mutiny; Gui's horse fell in the front line and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gui assaulted Caozhou and battled the Jin general Zheng Congyi for days on end. Food ran out and no relief came, yet his men did not waver. His horse collapsed in the fighting and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 囚至汴，金主壯其為人，誘以名爵，欲使揖，珪憤然曰：「吾身事大朝，官至光祿，復能受封他國耶！

translations.literal: Imprisoned and taken to Bian, the Jin ruler admired his character, tempted him with titles and rank, and wished to make him bow; Gui said in anger: "My person has served the Great Dynasty and risen to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—how could I again accept enfeoffment from another state!"
translations.idiomatic: Taken in chains to Bian, he impressed the Jin ruler, who offered him titles and asked him to bow. Gui flared up: "I have served the Great Dynasty and reached the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—how could I accept honors from another realm!"

sentences.zh: 假我一朝，當縛爾以獻。

translations.literal: "Give me but one morning, and I would bind you and present you as an offering."
translations.idiomatic: "Give me a single morning and I would bind you and hand you over as tribute."

sentences.zh: 」金主大怒，蒸殺于市，珪怡然就死，色不變。

translations.literal: " The Jin ruler was greatly enraged and had him steamed to death in the marketplace; Gui went to his death at ease, his countenance unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jin ruler flew into a rage and had him steamed alive in the market. Gui went to his death calmly, his face unaltered.

sentences.zh: 其麾下立社兗州祀焉。

translations.literal: His followers established a shrine in Yanzhou to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers set up a shrine in Yanzhou to honor him.

sentences.zh: 攸哈剌拔都，渤海人。

translations.literal: You Halabatu was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: You Halabatu came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 初名興哥，世農家，善射，以武斷鄉井。

translations.literal: His original name was Xingge; for generations his family were farmers; he was skilled at archery and ruled the countryside by force of arms.
translations.idiomatic: He was first called Xingge. His family had farmed for generations; he was a fine archer and dominated the countryside by force.

sentences.zh: 金末，避地大寧。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin he fled to take refuge in Daning.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin dynasty waned, he took refuge in Daning.

sentences.zh: 國兵至，出保高州富庶寨，射獵以食。

translations.literal: When the state's armies arrived, he went out to hold Fushu Stockade in Gaozhou and lived by hunting with bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies came he withdrew to Fushu Stockade in Gaozhou and lived by the hunt.

sentences.zh: 屢奪大營孳畜，又射死其追者。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he seized livestock from the great encampments and also shot dead those who pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he raided the main camps for livestock and shot down their pursuers.

sentences.zh: 國王木華黎率兵攻寨，寨破，奔高州，國兵圍城，下令曰：「能斬攸興哥首以降，則城中居民皆獲生。

translations.literal: Prince Muqali led troops to attack the stockade; when it fell, he fled to Gaozhou; the state's armies besieged the city and issued an order: "Whoever can cut off You Xingge's head and surrender—the city's inhabitants shall all be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Muqali stormed the stockade. When it fell Xingge fled to Gaozhou, which the imperial armies then besieged. They proclaimed: "Whoever brings us You Xingge's head and surrenders will save every soul in the city."

sentences.zh: 」守者召謂曰：「汝奇男子，吾寧忍斷汝首以獻，汝其往降乎！

translations.literal: " The defenders summoned him and said: "You are a remarkable man—how could we bear to cut off your head and offer it? You had better go and surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: " The garrison called him in and said: "You are a man of rare mettle. We cannot bring ourselves to take your head. You should go and submit."

sentences.zh: 不然，吾一城生靈，無噍類矣。

translations.literal: "Otherwise not one living soul in our whole city will be left."
translations.idiomatic: "Otherwise not a soul in this city will survive."

sentences.zh: 」興哥乃折矢出降。

translations.literal: " Xingge thereupon broke his arrow and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingge broke his arrow and came out to yield.

sentences.zh: 諸將怒，欲殺之，木華黎曰：「壯士也，留之為吾用。

translations.literal: The generals were angry and wished to kill him; Muqali said: "He is a brave man—keep him for my service."
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted him killed, but Muqali said: "This is a true warrior. Keep him for me."

sentences.zh: 」俾隸麾下。

translations.literal: " He was made to serve under his command.
translations.idiomatic: " He was placed in Muqali's own retinue.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎攻通州，獻計，一夕造砲三十、雲梯數十，附城，州將懼，出寶貨以降。

translations.literal: Following Muqali in the attack on Tongzhou, he offered a plan: in one night they built thirty catapults and several dozen cloud ladders, brought them up to the wall, and the prefectural commander grew afraid and came out with treasures to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Muqali against Tongzhou and proposed a plan: in a single night they built thirty catapults and dozens of siege ladders, pressed them to the walls, and the prefect surrendered with his treasure.

sentences.zh: 木華黎命興哥恣取之，興哥獨取良馬三，以賞兵士。

translations.literal: Muqali ordered Xingge to take whatever he pleased; Xingge took only three fine horses and used them to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali told Xingge to take what he wanted. He took only three good horses and gave them to his men as rewards.

sentences.zh: 木華黎以其功聞太祖，賜名哈剌拔都。

translations.literal: Muqali reported his merit to the Taizu, who bestowed on him the name Halabatu.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali reported his deeds to Taizu, who granted him the name Halabatu.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎略地燕南，為先鋒，至大名，金將徒單登城督戰，哈剌拔都射之，中左目，其部將開門南奔，追殺將盡。

translations.literal: Following Muqali in the pacification of the lands south of Yan, he served as vanguard; reaching Daming, the Jin general Tushan mounted the wall to direct the battle; Halabatu shot him and struck his left eye; his subordinate commanders opened the gate and fled south; they were pursued and nearly all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Muqali through southern Yan as vanguard. At Daming the Jin general Tushan stood on the wall to direct the fight. Halabatu shot him in the left eye. The garrison commanders opened the gates and fled south; the pursuers cut down nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 論功，賜金符，充隨營監察。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was given a golden tally and appointed camp inspector attached to the army.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received a golden tally and was made camp inspector on the field army staff.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，授金虎符、龍虎衛上將軍、河東北路兵馬都元帥，鎮太原。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year he was given a golden tiger tally, made General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, and appointed marshal of the armies of Hedong North Circuit, garrisoning Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he received a golden tiger tally, the rank of General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, and the marshalship of the Hedong North Circuit, with Taiyuan as his seat.

sentences.zh: 時太原新破，哈剌拔都修城池，繕兵甲，招降屬邑，市肆不改，遠近聞之，皆相率來歸。

translations.literal: At that time Taiyuan had just been taken; Halabatu repaired the walls and moats, put arms and armor in order, summoned surrender from subordinate districts, and left the markets unchanged; when near and far heard of this, all came in groups to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan had only just fallen when Halabatu rebuilt the walls, re-equipped the troops, and called in the surrounding districts. He left the markets undisturbed, and people from far and near came over in droves.

sentences.zh: 嘗微服夜出，聞民間語曰：「吾屬父母子女相失矣，死者不可復生，生者無以為贖，奈何！

translations.literal: Once he went out at night in plain dress and heard people in the streets say: "We have lost parents, children, husbands and wives; the dead cannot live again, and the living have no means to ransom them—what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: One night he went out in disguise and overheard townspeople saying: "Families are torn apart—parents from children, husbands from wives. The dead cannot return, and we have nothing with which to ransom the living. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」明日，下令軍中，凡俘獲有親者聽贖，無貲者官為贖之，民得完聚者衆。

translations.literal: " The next day he issued an order in the army: wherever captives had kin who wished to ransom them, ransoms were permitted; those without means had the state ransom them; many among the people were able to be reunited whole.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he ordered that any captive with kin might be ransomed, and that the government would pay when families could not. Great numbers of people were reunited.

sentences.zh: 庚辰二月，金梁知府立西風寨，奪居民耕牛，民群訴之，哈剌拔都領數騎，追殺梁知府，梟首西門，驅耕牛還。

translations.literal: In the second month of the gengchen year the Jin prefect Liang set up Xifeng Stockade and seized the peasants' plough oxen; the people came in crowds to complain; Halabatu led a few horsemen, pursued and killed Prefect Liang, displayed his head at the west gate, and drove the plough oxen back.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the gengchen year the Jin prefect Liang seized a stockade called Xifeng and took the farmers' oxen. When the people petitioned in a body, Halabatu rode out with a handful of men, ran Liang down and killed him, hung his head at the west gate, and drove the oxen home.

sentences.zh: 木華黎由葭州渡河西行，哈剌拔都迎之，道破隰州及懸窯、地洞諸寨。

translations.literal: Muqali crossed the Yellow River westward from Jiazhou; Halabatu went to meet him and on the way broke Xizhou and the stockades of Xuanyao, Didong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali crossed the Yellow River west from Jiazhou. Halabatu met him on the road and along the way reduced Xizhou and the stockades at Xuanyao, Didong, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 辛巳三月，金兵攻壽陽縣王胡莊，垂破，時左右裨將各分兵守險，城中見卒不滿百，哈剌拔都夜半引甲騎十餘人救之，道三交，見金兵舉烽東、西兩山，哈剌拔都趨之，大戰。

translations.literal: In the third month of the xinsi year Jin troops attacked Wanghu Manor in Shouyang County, which was on the verge of falling; at the time the left and right deputy commanders had each divided their forces to hold dangerous passes, and the visible garrison in the city was fewer than a hundred; Halabatu at midnight led a dozen or so armored horsemen to the rescue; on the road at Sanjiao he saw Jin troops raising beacon fires on the eastern and western hills; Halabatu hastened thither and fought a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the xinsi year the Jin assaulted Wanghu Manor in Shouyang County, which was near collapse. The deputy commanders had split their forces to hold the passes, and fewer than a hundred men remained in the city. Halabatu rode out after midnight with a dozen armored horsemen. At Sanjiao he saw Jin signal fires on the hills east and west and charged into a fierce battle.

sentences.zh: 天將明，金兵遁去，擣太原之虛，由西門俘獲哈剌拔都家屬。

translations.literal: As dawn was near the Jin troops fled; they feigned an attack on Taiyuan and through the west gate captured Halabatu's family.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the Jin withdrew, feinted against Taiyuan, and through the west gate seized Halabatu's household.

sentences.zh: 哈剌拔都聞之，徑趨西山，復奪以還。

translations.literal: When Halabatu heard of it he went straight to the western hills, recovered them, and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, he rode straight for the western hills, retook his family, and brought them home.

sentences.zh: 五月，金趙權府率兵三萬圍太原，哈剌拔都將騎三十，出西門，令騎曳柴揚塵，聲言曰：「國兵三萬至矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Jin commander Zhao Quanfu led thirty thousand troops to besiege Taiyuan; Halabatu took thirty horsemen out the west gate, ordered the riders to drag brushwood and raise dust, and proclaimed aloud: "The state's army of thirty thousand has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Jin commander Zhao Quanfu besieged Taiyuan with thirty thousand men. Halabatu led thirty horsemen out the west gate, had them drag brushwood to raise dust, and shouted: "Thirty thousand imperial troops are here!"

sentences.zh: 」金兵懼，潰去。

translations.literal: " The Jin troops were afraid and broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jin panicked and broke ranks.

sentences.zh: 癸未，金馬武京來攻太谷縣桑梓寨，哈剌拔都設伏于險，將輕騎衝其陣，伏發，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year the Jin commander Ma Wujing came to attack Sangzi Stockade in Taigu County; Halabatu set an ambush in a defile, led light cavalry in a charge on their battle line, the ambush sprang, and they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year the Jin general Ma Wujing attacked Sangzi Stockade in Taigu County. Halabatu laid an ambush in the hills, led light cavalry in a frontal charge, sprang the trap, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時太原諸邑皆平，唯石家昂及盂州陵井寨、忻州清泉寨為唇齒，皆未下。

translations.literal: At that time all the districts around Taiyuan were pacified; only Shijia'ang and Lingjing Stockade in Yuzhou and Qingquan Stockade in Xinzhou stood in mutual support like lips and teeth, and none had yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By then every district around Taiyuan had submitted except Shijia'ang, Lingjing Stockade in Yuzhou, and Qingquan Stockade in Xinzhou, which backed one another and still held out.

sentences.zh: 甲申十月，將兵至陵井，遣卒叩寨門，詐曰納糧芻，守者弗悟，門啟，徑入，蹂踐之，衆潰，其酋長走石家昂，遂平陵井寨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the jiashen year he led troops to Lingjing, sent soldiers to knock on the stockade gate, and falsely said they were delivering grain and fodder; the defenders did not perceive the ruse, the gate opened, they entered straight in, trampled the place, the multitude broke, the chieftain fled to Shijia'ang, and Lingjing Stockade was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the jiashen year he marched on Lingjing and sent men to knock at the gate, claiming they brought grain and fodder. The guards opened the gate unsuspecting. His troops poured in, overran the stockade, and routed the garrison. The chieftain fled to Shijia'ang, and Lingjing fell.

sentences.zh: 乙酉二月，清泉寨酋長王殼降，石家昂亦降。

translations.literal: In the second month of the yiyou year the chieftain of Qingquan Stockade, Wang Ke, surrendered, and Shijia'ang also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the yiyou year Wang Ke, chieftain of Qingquan Stockade, submitted, and Shijia'ang followed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥五月，姦人夜獻太原東門于武仙，仙引兵入，哈剌拔都鏖戰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the dinghai year traitors by night offered Taiyuan's east gate to Wuxian; Wuxian led troops in, and Halabatu fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the dinghai year traitors opened Taiyuan's east gate by night to Wuxian, who marched in. Halabatu fought hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 仙兵大至，諸將自城外呼曰：「攸哈剌拔都，汝當出！

translations.literal: Wuxian's troops came in great force; the generals called from outside the wall: "You Halabatu, you ought to come out!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuxian's army swelled. His generals shouted from beyond the walls: "You Halabatu—come out!"

sentences.zh: 」哈剌拔都曰：「真定史天倪，平陽李守忠，隰州田雄，皆失守矣，我又棄太原，將何面目見主上及國王乎！

translations.literal: " Halabatu said: "Shi Tianni of Zhending, Li Shouzhong of Pingyang, and Tian Xiong of Xizhou have all lost their posts—if I too abandon Taiyuan, with what face shall I see the sovereign and the prince!"
translations.idiomatic: " Halabatu answered: "Shi Tianni at Zhending, Li Shouzhong at Pingyang, and Tian Xiong at Xizhou have all lost their cities. If I abandon Taiyuan too, how can I face the emperor or the prince?"

sentences.zh: 家屬任公等所俘，哈剌拔都誓與城同存亡。

translations.literal: His family had been captured by Duke Ren and others; Halabatu swore to live or die with the city.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been taken by Duke Ren and the rest, but Halabatu swore to stand or fall with the city.

sentences.zh: 」遂歿于陣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: " He fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其子幼，命其表弟王七十復立太原。

translations.literal: The Taizu, because his son was young, ordered his cousin Wang Qishi to re-establish Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son was still a child, Taizu appointed his cousin Wang Qishi to restore order at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 己丑，攻鳳翔府，中砲死。

translations.literal: In the jichou year he attacked Fengxiang Prefecture and was killed by a catapult stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the jichou year he assaulted Fengxiang Prefecture and was killed by a catapult shot.

sentences.zh: 哈剌拔都長子忙兀台，嗣鎮太原。

translations.literal: Halabatu's eldest son Mangutai succeeded him in garrisoning Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Halabatu's eldest son Mangutai succeeded him as commander at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 任志，潞州人。

translations.literal: Ren Zhi was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhi came from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲戊寅，太師、國王木華黎略地至潞州，志首迎降，國王授以虎符，俾充元帥，收輯山寨。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year the Grand Preceptor and prince Muqali, in pacifying the territory, reached Luzhou; Zhi was the first to welcome him and surrender; the prince gave him a tiger tally and made him marshal, charging him to gather in the mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali reached Luzhou on campaign. Zhi was the first to submit. The prince gave him a tiger tally, made him marshal, and set him to bring in the mountain strongholds.

sentences.zh: 數與金兵戰，比有功。

translations.literal: He fought the Jin troops many times and each time had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Jin repeatedly and won credit each time.

sentences.zh: 金嘗擒其長子如山以招之，曰：「降則爾子得生，不降則死。

translations.literal: The Jin once captured his eldest son Rushan to entice him, saying: "If you surrender your son will live; if you do not, he will die."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin once seized his eldest son Rushan to win him over, saying: "Surrender and your son lives; refuse and he dies."

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「我為大朝之帥，豈愛一子！

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "I am a commander of the Great Dynasty—how could I cherish one son!"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi replied: "I am a commander of the Great Dynasty. Would I spare one son for that?"

sentences.zh: 」親射其子殪之。

translations.literal: " He personally shot his son and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He took bow in hand and shot his son dead himself.

sentences.zh: 木華黎嘗召諸將議事，志亦預徵，道經武安，其縣已反為金，志死之。

translations.literal: Muqali once summoned the generals to discuss affairs; Zhi was also among those called; on the road he passed through Wu'an, whose county had already rebelled and gone over to the Jin, and Zhi died there.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali once called the generals to council, and Zhi was summoned too. Passing through Wu'an, he found the county had gone over to the Jin, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 國王閔之，令其子存襲。

translations.literal: The prince mourned him and had his son Cun succeed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The prince mourned him and had his son Cun inherit his command.

sentences.zh: 庚寅歲，金將武仙攻潞州，存戰死。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year the Jin general Wuxian attacked Luzhou, and Cun died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year the Jin general Wuxian attacked Luzhou, and Cun was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 辛卯正月，有旨潞州元帥任存妻孥家屬，令有司廩給，仍賜第以居之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the xinmao year an order went forth that the wife, children, and household of Ren Cun, marshal of Luzhou, were to receive grain rations from the authorities, and a residence was granted for them to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the xinmao year an edict directed that the wife, children, and household of Luzhou marshal Ren Cun be maintained on government rations and given a house to live in.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以存父子死事，子立尚幼，先官其姪成為潞州長官，待立長而還授之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, because father and son Cun had died in service and the son Li was still young, his nephew Cheng was first given office as chief of Luzhou, to hold it until Li grew up and the post would be returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, because father and son had died in service and Li was still a child, his nephew Cheng was appointed chief of Luzhou until Li came of age, when the post would revert to him.

sentences.zh: 成卒，授立潞州長官，佩金符。

translations.literal: When Cheng died, Li was appointed chief of Luzhou and wore a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died, Li was made chief of Luzhou with a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 後歷澤州尹，遷陳州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as prefect of Zezhou, was transferred to Chenzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Zezhou, was transferred to Chenzhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 耶律忒末，契丹人。

translations.literal: Yelü Teme was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Teme was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 父丑哥仕遼為都統，遼亡，不屈節，夫婦俱死焉。

translations.literal: His father Chouge had served the Liao as commander-in-chief; when the Liao perished he would not bend his integrity, and husband and wife both died there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chouge had been a commander-in-chief under the Liao. When the dynasty fell he refused to submit, and he and his wife died together.

sentences.zh: 金主憫其忠義，授忒末都統。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler pitied their loyalty and righteousness and appointed Teme commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor, moved by their loyalty, made Teme commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，國兵至，金徙于汴，忒末及子天祐率衆三萬內附，授帥府監軍，天祐招討使，從元帥史天倪略趙州平棘、欒城、元氏、柏鄉、贊皇、臨城等縣，籍其民五千餘，置吏安輯焉。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year the state's armies arrived and the Jin moved to Bian; Teme and his son Tianyou led thirty thousand men in internal submission; Teme was appointed army supervisor of the marshal's headquarters and Tianyou pacification commissioner; following the marshal Shi Tianni they pacified Pingji, Luancheng, Yuanshi, Baixiang, Zanhuang, Lincheng, and other counties of Zhaozhou, registered more than five thousand of their people, and set officials to settle and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year the imperial armies arrived and the Jin court withdrew to Bian. Teme and his son Tianyou brought thirty thousand men over to the Yuan side. Teme was made army supervisor at the marshal's headquarters and Tianyou pacification commissioner. With Marshal Shi Tianni they took Pingji, Luancheng, Yuanshi, Baixiang, Zanhuang, Lincheng, and other counties in Zhaozhou, registered more than five thousand households, and appointed officials to govern them.

sentences.zh: 歲辛巳，太師木華黎統領諸道兵馬，承制加忒末洺州等路征行元帥，與天祐略邢、洺、磁、相、懷、孟，昭花馬劉元帥，有功。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year the Grand Preceptor Muqali commanded the armies of all circuits; acting by commission he further appointed Teme campaign marshal of the circuits of Mingzhou and others; with Tianyou he pacified Xing, Ming, Ci, Xiang, Huai, and Meng, and together with Marshal Liu Zhaohuama had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year Grand Preceptor Muqali took command of the armies of every circuit and, acting under warrant, promoted Teme to campaign marshal of the Mingzhou circuit and others. With Tianyou he subdued Xing, Ming, Ci, Xiang, Huai, and Meng, and with Marshal Liu Zhaohuama won distinction.

sentences.zh: 木華黎又承制授忒末真定路安撫使、洺州元帥，進兵臨澤潞，降其民六千餘戶，以功遷河北西路安撫使，兼澤潞元帥府事。

translations.literal: Muqali again acting by commission appointed Teme pacification commissioner of Zhending Circuit and marshal of Mingzhou; he advanced troops to the borders of Ze and Lu, reduced more than six thousand households of the people, and for his merit was transferred to pacification commissioner of Hebei West Circuit, concurrently holding the affairs of the Ze-Lu Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali further appointed him, by warrant, pacification commissioner of Zhending and marshal of Mingzhou. He marched on Ze and Lu, brought over more than six thousand households, and was promoted to pacification commissioner of Hebei West Circuit with concurrent charge of the Ze-Lu marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 壬午，致仕，退居真定。

translations.literal: In the renwu year he retired from office and withdrew to dwell in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year he retired and lived out his days at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 天祐襲職，從天倪攻取益都諸城，略滄、棣，得戶七千，兼滄、棣州達魯花赤，佩金符。

translations.literal: Tianyou succeeded to his post, followed Tianni in attacking and taking the cities of Yidu, reduced Cang and Di, obtained seven thousand households, and concurrently served as darughachi of Cang and Di prefectures, wearing the golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou succeeded to his father's post, followed Tianni in the capture of the Yidu cities, and reduced Cang and Di, gaining seven thousand households. He also served as darughachi of Cang and Di prefectures and wore the golden tally.

sentences.zh: 時金鹽山衛鎮鹽場未下，天祐以計克之，歲運鹽四千席，以佐軍儲。

translations.literal: At that time the salt works of the Jin Yanshan Guard garrison town had not yet submitted; Tianyou took them by stratagem and each year transported four thousand bundles of salt to supplement military stores.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin salt works at the Yanshan Guard garrison had not yet submitted; Tianyou took them by stratagem and each year shipped four thousand bundles of salt to supplement the army's supplies.

sentences.zh: 甲申，攻大名，拔之。

translations.literal: In the jiashen year he attacked Daming and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiashen year he attacked Daming and captured it.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，金降將武仙據真定以叛，殺守將史天倪。

translations.literal: In the yiyou year the Jin defector Wu Xian seized Zhending in rebellion and killed the defending commander Shi Tianni.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiyou year the Jin defector Wu Xian seized Zhending in revolt and killed the defending commander Shi Tianni.

sentences.zh: 忒末父子夜踰城而出，將以聞，會天倪弟天澤還自北京，遇諸滿城，合蒙古諸軍南與賊戰，走武仙，復真定。

translations.literal: Father and son Temei by night climbed over the wall and went out, intending to report the matter. Just then Tianni's younger brother Tianze returned from Beiping, met them outside the full city, united the Mongol armies southward to fight the rebels, put Wu Xian to flight, and recovered Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Temei and his son slipped over the wall by night to bring word of the revolt. Tianni's brother Tianze was returning from Beiping, met them outside the city, united the Mongol forces, drove south against the rebels, routed Wu Xian, and retook Zhending.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以天澤襲兄爵，而以天祐鎮趙州。

translations.literal: The court had Tianze succeed to his elder brother's rank and stationed Tianyou at Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court had Tianze succeed to his brother's rank and posted Tianyou as garrison commander at Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，仙復犯真定，天澤潛師出藁城，忒末與其妻石抹氏，及家孥在真定者，皆陷焉。

translations.literal: The next year Wu Xian again attacked Zhending. Tianze led troops secretly out from Gaocheng. Temei, his wife Lady Shimota, and all the family members in Zhending were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Xian attacked Zhending again. Tianze marched secretly from Gaocheng, and Temei, his wife Lady Shimota, and every member of their household in the city were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 仙遣其僕劉攬兒，持書誘天祐曰：「汝能誅趙州官吏以降，當活汝父母，仍授汝元帥；

translations.literal: Wu Xian sent his servant Liu Lan'er with a letter to entice Tianyou, saying: "If you can kill the Zhao Prefecture officials and surrender, your parents will be spared and you will still be made marshal;"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian sent his servant Liu Lan'er with a letter tempting Tianyou: "If you kill the Zhao Prefecture officials and surrender, your parents will live and you will be made marshal;"

sentences.zh: 不爾，盡烹之。

translations.literal: "If not, they will all be boiled alive."
translations.idiomatic: "Refuse, and they will all be put in the cauldron."

sentences.zh: 」忒末密令攬兒語天祐曰：「仙賊狡猾，汝所知也，毋以我故，墮其機阱，以虧忠節。

translations.literal: Temei secretly ordered Lan'er to tell Tianyou: "The rebel Wu Xian is cunning—as you know. Do not for my sake fall into his trap and compromise your loyalty and integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Temei secretly told Lan'er to say to Tianyou: "You know how cunning the rebel Wu Xian is. Do not for my sake fall into his trap and betray your duty."

sentences.zh: 且忠孝難兩全，汝能固守，不失國家大計，我視刀鋸甘如蜜矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, loyalty and filial piety are hard to fulfill together. If you can hold firm and not fail the state's great plan, I shall regard blade and saw as sweet as honey.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be satisfied. If you hold the line and do not fail the state's purpose, I shall welcome blade and saw as gladly as honey.

sentences.zh: 」天祐慟哭承命，馳至藁城，以賊書示天澤。

translations.literal: Tianyou wept bitterly, accepted the charge, galloped to Gaocheng, and showed the rebel's letter to Tianze.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou wept as he accepted his father's charge, rode hard to Gaocheng, and showed Wu Xian's letter to Tianze.

sentences.zh: 天澤曰：「王陵之事，照耀史冊，汝能遵父命，忠誠許國，功不在王陵下。

translations.literal: Tianze said: "Wang Ling's deed shines in the historical records. If you can follow your father's command, loyally devote yourself to the state, your achievement will not fall below Wang Ling's."
translations.idiomatic: Tianze said: "Wang Ling's deed shines in the histories. If you obey your father's command and devote yourself loyally to the state, your achievement will not fall short of his."

sentences.zh: 」天祐乃趨還趙壁，率衆殊死戰，仙怒，盡殺忒末家一十八人。

translations.literal: Tianyou then hurried back to the Zhao ramparts, led the masses in a fight to the death. Wu Xian was enraged and killed all eighteen members of Temei's household.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou raced back to the Zhao defenses and led his men in a desperate fight. Enraged, Wu Xian put all eighteen members of Temei's household to death.

sentences.zh: 戰于欒城、元氏、高邑、柏鄉，仙兵屢挫。

translations.literal: Battles were fought at Luancheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, and Baixiang, and Wu Xian's troops were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at Luancheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, and Baixiang, and Wu Xian's forces suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 監軍張林密搆仙黨，啟關納賊。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Zhang Lin secretly colluded with Wu Xian's faction, opened the gate, and admitted the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Zhang Lin secretly conspired with Wu Xian's faction, opened the gates, and let the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 天祐倉皇巷戰，手殺數十人，身被十餘瘡，斬關出，復收散卒圍城。

translations.literal: Tianyou fought desperately in the lanes, personally killed several tens of men, received more than ten wounds on his body, cut his way out through the gate, and again gathered scattered troops to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou fought desperately in the streets, killed dozens of men with his own hand, took more than ten wounds, cut his way out through the gate, and rallied scattered troops to besiege the city again.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，賊棄城走，追至藁城，會天澤兵夾擊，殺林。

translations.literal: In the dinghai year the rebels abandoned the city and fled. They were pursued to Gaocheng; Tianze's troops joined in a pincer attack and Zhang Lin was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year the rebels abandoned the city and fled. Pursued to Gaocheng, they were caught in a pincer by Tianze's troops and Zhang Lin was killed.

sentences.zh: 加奉國上將軍、洺州征行元帥，兼趙州安撫使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Upholds the State, campaigning marshal of Mozhou, and concurrently pacification commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Upholds the State, campaign marshal of Mozhou, and concurrent pacification commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以傷憊致仕，居趙，卒。

translations.literal: Worn by his wounds, he retired from office, dwelt at Zhao, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Broken by his wounds, he retired, lived at Zhao, and died there.

sentences.zh: 孫世枻，朝列大夫、江西榷茶都轉運使。

translations.literal: His grandson Shi Jie was Court Gentleman for Attendance and chief transport commissioner for the Jiangxi tea monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shi Jie served as Court Gentleman for Attendance and chief transport commissioner for the Jiangxi tea monopoly.

sentences.zh: 伯八，晃合丹氏。

translations.literal: Bo Ba was of the Huanghedan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ba belonged to the Huanghedan clan.

sentences.zh: 祖明里也赤哥，嘗隸太祖帳下。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mingliye Chige had once served under the Great Ancestor's tent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mingliye Chige had once served in the Great Ancestor's retinue.

sentences.zh: 初，怯列王可罕與太祖為鄰國，誓相親好，既而敗盟，與其子先髡潛謀，欲襲太祖，因遣使通問，許以女妻太祖弟合撒兒。

translations.literal: At first Prince Kereyid Khan was a neighboring state to the Great Ancestor and swore mutual friendship. Later he broke the covenant and secretly plotted with his son Senggum to attack the Great Ancestor. He therefore sent envoys with greetings, promising to give his daughter in marriage to the Great Ancestor's younger brother Qasar.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Kereyid khan was the Great Ancestor's neighbor and ally by oath. Later he broke faith and secretly plotted with his son Senggum to ambush the Great Ancestor, sending envoys to propose marriage between his daughter and the Great Ancestor's brother Qasar.

sentences.zh: 至期，太祖欲往，明里也赤哥疑其詐，諫止之。

translations.literal: When the day arrived the Great Ancestor wished to go. Mingliye Chige suspected treachery and remonstrated to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came the Great Ancestor meant to go, but Mingliye Chige suspected a trap and persuaded him not to.

sentences.zh: 王可罕知謀泄，遂謀入寇，後為太祖所滅。

translations.literal: The prince-khan learned the plot had leaked and therefore planned an invasion; later he was destroyed by the Great Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When the khan learned the plot had been exposed he prepared to invade, but in the end the Great Ancestor destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 父脫倫闍里必，扈從太祖征西域，累立奇功。

translations.literal: His father Tolun Jarlibi followed in attendance on the Great Ancestor in the western campaign and repeatedly achieved extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tolun Jarlibi followed the Great Ancestor on the western campaigns and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以伯八舊臣子孫，擢為萬戶，命領諸部軍馬屯守欠欠州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, because Bo Ba was a descendant of an old minister, he was promoted to commander of ten thousand households and ordered to lead the armies of the various tribes in garrison at Qianqianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, Bo Ba was raised to commander of ten thousand households as a descendant of an old minister and ordered to garrison Qianqianzhou with the forces of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，親王昔列吉、脫鐵木兒叛，奔海都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of the Zhiyuan era the princes Shiregi and Totemur rebelled and fled to Kaidu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 12 the princes Shiregi and Totemur rose in rebellion and fled to Kaidu.

sentences.zh: 伯八以聞，且願提兵往討之，未得命，為彼所襲，死焉。

translations.literal: Bo Ba reported it and also asked to lead troops to attack them. Before he received orders he was raided by them and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ba reported the revolt and asked to lead troops against them, but before orders came he was attacked and killed.

sentences.zh: 脫鐵木兒虜其二子八剌、不蘭奚，分置左右，居歲餘，待之頗厚。

translations.literal: Totemur captured his two sons Bala and Bulanxi, placed them on his left and right, and for more than a year treated them quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: Totemur captured his sons Bala and Bulanxi, kept them at his side, and for more than a year treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 八剌陰結脫鐵木兒近侍也里伯禿，謀報父仇，後為也伯里禿家人泄其謀。

translations.literal: Bala secretly joined with Totemur's close attendant Yelibatu to plan vengeance for his father. Later a member of Yelibatu's household revealed the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Bala secretly won over Totemur's attendant Yelibatu to plot revenge for his father, but a member of Yelibatu's household exposed the scheme.

sentences.zh: 八剌知事不成，將家族南奔，脫鐵木兒遣騎追之，至一河，八剌馬驚，不能渡，回拒之，射中數人，力窮，兄弟就擒。

translations.literal: Bala knew the affair would not succeed and was about to flee south with his clan. Totemur sent horsemen in pursuit. At a river Bala's horse panicked and could not cross. He turned back to resist, shot several men, but when his strength was exhausted the brothers were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the plot had failed, Bala fled south with his family. Totemur's horsemen overtook him at a river; his horse panicked and could not cross. He turned to fight, shot down several pursuers, but when his strength gave out he and his brother were taken.

sentences.zh: 脫鐵木兒責之曰：「我待汝厚甚，而汝反為此耶！

translations.literal: Totemur rebuked him, saying: "I treated you very generously—yet you turn to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Totemur rebuked him: "I treated you generously—yet you do this!"

sentences.zh: 」八剌曰：「汝背叛君上，害我父，掠我親屬，我誓欲殺汝，以報君父之讎，今力窮被執，從汝所為！

translations.literal: Bala said: "You betrayed your sovereign, killed my father, and seized my kin. I swore to kill you to avenge my sovereign and father. Now my strength is spent and I am captured—do as you will!"
translations.idiomatic: Bala said: "You betrayed your lord, killed my father, and seized my kin. I swore to kill you to avenge my sovereign and father. My strength is spent and I am your prisoner—do as you please!"

sentences.zh: 」逼令跪，不屈，以鐵撾碎其膝，終不跪，與弟不闌奚同被害。

translations.literal: They forced him to kneel but he would not yield. With iron clubs they shattered his knees, yet he still would not kneel. He and his younger brother Bulanxi were killed together.
translations.idiomatic: They forced him to kneel, but he refused. They smashed his knees with iron clubs, yet he still would not kneel. He and his brother Bulanxi were put to death together.

sentences.zh: 幼子何都兀赤，官至河北河南道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: His youngest son Hodu'uchi reached the office of surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Hodu'uchi rose to surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 合剌普華，岳璘帖木爾子也。

translations.literal: Helapuhua was the son of Yuelintiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: Helapuhua was a son of Yuelintiemuer.

sentences.zh: 幼侍母奧敦氏居益都，嘗歎曰：「幼而不學，有不墮吾宗者乎！

translations.literal: In youth he attended his mother Lady Aodun while dwelling at Yidu and once sighed, saying: "If one does not study in youth, is there not one who will bring down our clan!"
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he lived with his mother Lady Aodun at Yidu and once sighed: "If a man does not study in youth, will he not bring shame on our house!"

sentences.zh: 」父時以斷事官建牙保定，合剌普華往白其志。

translations.literal: His father was then establishing his headquarters at Baoding as a judicial officer. Helapuhua went to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: His father was then serving as a judicial officer with his headquarters at Baoding, and Helapuhua went to tell him of his resolve.

sentences.zh: 父奇之，俾習畏兀書及經史，記誦精敏，出於天性。

translations.literal: His father marveled at him and had him study Uighur script and the classics and histories. His memorization was keen and swift, arising from his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: His father was impressed and had him study Uighur script and the classics and histories. His memory was quick and sharp by nature.

sentences.zh: 李璮畔，其母攜季子脫烈普華避地登、萊間，音問隔絕，號泣徹晝夜。

translations.literal: When Li Tan rebelled, his mother took the youngest son Tuoliepuhua to seek refuge between Deng and Lai. Word was cut off, and he wept and wailed through day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled, his mother fled with the youngest son Tuoliepuhua to the Deng and Lai region. Cut off from news of them, he wept day and night.

sentences.zh: 繼從從叔父撒吉思平賊山東，卒奉其母以歸。

translations.literal: Later he followed his father's younger cousin Sagis in pacifying the rebels in Shandong and at last brought his mother back in honor.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed his father's cousin Sagis in pacifying Shandong and at last brought his mother home in safety.

sentences.zh: 撒吉思深加器重，自謂其才不及，言於世祖，召給宿衛。

translations.literal: Sagis greatly valued him, saying himself that his own talent did not match Helapuhua's, and spoke of him to Emperor Shizu, who summoned him to serve in the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sagis held him in high esteem, declaring his own talent inferior, and recommended him to Emperor Shizu, who summoned him to the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗以事至益都，於四腳山下置廣興、商山二冶，以勞授金符，為商山鐵冶都提舉；

translations.literal: Once on business he went to Yidu and at the foot of Four-Legged Mountain established the Guangxing and Shangshan ironworks. For his service he was granted the golden tally and made chief intendant of the Shangshan ironworks;
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Yidu he established the Guangxing and Shangshan ironworks at the foot of Four-Legged Mountain. For his service he received the golden tally and was made chief intendant of the Shangshan ironworks;

sentences.zh: 未及代，以職讓其弟。

translations.literal: before his term ended he yielded the post to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: but before his term ended he yielded the post to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 時兵南伐，餽運繁興，被選為行都漕運使，帥諸翼兵萬五千人，從事飛輓。

translations.literal: At that time the army was campaigning south and transport was urgently needed. He was chosen as acting chief transport commissioner, commanding fifteen thousand troops of the various wings to engage in rapid supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: With the southern campaigns under way and supply lines strained, he was chosen acting chief transport commissioner and led fifteen thousand wing troops in rapid grain transport.

sentences.zh: 江南平，上疏言：「親肺腑，禮大臣，以存國家之體。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan region was pacified he submitted a memorial saying: "Cherish those of one's own flesh and blood, honor great ministers—to preserve the state's proper form."
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified he submitted a memorial: "Cherish the imperial kin, honor great ministers—to preserve the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 興學校，獎名節，以勵天下之士。

translations.literal: "Establish schools, reward integrity and reputation—to encourage the scholars of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: "Establish schools and reward integrity—to encourage the scholars of the realm."

sentences.zh: 正名分，嚴考課，以定百官之法。

translations.literal: "Rectify ranks and titles, tighten examinations and assessments—to fix the law for the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: "Clarify ranks and tighten examinations—to fix the standards for officials."

sentences.zh: 通泉幣，却貢獻，以厚生民之本。

translations.literal: "Circulate currency, reject excessive tribute—to strengthen the foundation of the people's livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: "Circulate currency and curb excessive tribute—to strengthen the people's livelihood."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「江南新附，宜招舊族，力穡通商，弛征薄入，以撫馴其民，不然，恐尚煩宵旰之慮。

translations.literal: He also said: "The newly submitted Jiangnan should have its old clans summoned, agriculture and commerce encouraged, levies relaxed and collections lightened, to soothe and tame its people—otherwise I fear it may still trouble Your Majesty's sleepless cares."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "The newly submitted south should have its old families recalled, farming and trade encouraged, and taxes eased—to win over the people. Otherwise Your Majesty may yet lose sleep over it."

sentences.zh: 」帝多采用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 屬漕米二十萬，繇邗溝達于河，舟覆，損十之一，而又每斛視都斛虧三升。

translations.literal: He was charged with two hundred thousand piculs of transport grain, conveyed by the Hangou Canal to reach the Yellow River. Boats capsized and one tenth was lost; moreover each picul was short three sheng compared with the capital standard picul.
translations.idiomatic: He was responsible for two hundred thousand piculs of grain, sent by the Hangou Canal to the Yellow River. Boats capsized and a tenth was lost; moreover each picul fell three sheng short of the capital standard.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬專政，責償舟人。

translations.literal: At that time Ahmad held sole power and demanded compensation from the boatmen.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad then held sole power and demanded that the boatmen make good the loss.

sentences.zh: 合剌普華伏闕抗言：「量之踦贏，出於元降，而水道之虞，非人力所及。

translations.literal: Helapuhua prostrated himself before the palace gate and protested: "Short measure and surplus or deficit arise from the original allocation, while the hazards of the water route are beyond human control."
translations.idiomatic: Helapuhua knelt before the palace gate and protested: "Short measure comes from the original allocation, and the hazards of the waterways are beyond human control."

sentences.zh: 且彼雖罄其家，不足以償，苟朝廷必不任虧損，臣獨當其辜。

translations.literal: "Moreover, though they exhaust their households it would not suffice to repay. If the court will certainly not accept any loss, I alone shall bear the guilt."
translations.idiomatic: "Even if they sold everything they owned it would not cover the loss. If the court will accept no shortfall, let me bear the blame alone."

sentences.zh: 」詔勿治。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the matter not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬憤之，乃出合剌普華為寧海路達魯花赤，後遷江西宣慰使，未至官，改廣東都轉運鹽使，兼領諸番市舶。

translations.literal: Ahmad was angry and therefore sent Helapuhua out as darughachi of Ninghai Circuit. Later he was transferred to Jiangxi pacification commissioner, but before he took office was changed to Guangdong chief salt transport commissioner, concurrently overseeing the maritime trade of the various foreign merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad, furious, posted Helapuhua as darughachi of Ninghai Circuit. He was later transferred to Jiangxi pacification commissioner, but before taking office was reassigned as Guangdong chief salt transport commissioner, with oversight of foreign maritime trade.

sentences.zh: 時盜梗鹽法，陳良臣扇東莞、香山、惠州負販之徒萬人為亂，江西行省命與招討使荅失蠻討捕之，先驅斬渠魁，以訊馘告，躬抵賊巢，招誘餘黨復業，仍條言鹽法之不便者，悉除其害。

translations.literal: At that time bandits obstructed the salt laws. Chen Liangchen incited ten thousand peddlers of Dongguan, Xiangshan, and Huizhou to rebel. The Jiangxi Branch Secretariat ordered him, together with the pacification commissioner Qashin, to pursue and capture them. He first drove forward and beheaded the ringleaders, reported the interrogation and heads taken, personally reached the bandit lair, summoned and induced the remaining followers to return to their occupations, and also listed the inconveniences of the salt laws, removing all such harms.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were disrupting the salt laws when Chen Liangchen stirred ten thousand peddlers in Dongguan, Xiangshan, and Huizhou to revolt. The Jiangxi Branch Secretariat ordered Helapuhua and the pacification commissioner Qashin to suppress them. He led the van, beheaded the ringleaders, reported the results, went in person to the rebels' lair, induced the remainder to return to honest work, and listed every abuse in the salt laws, abolishing them all.

sentences.zh: 按察使脫歡大為姦利，遂奏罷之。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner Tuohuan greatly practiced corruption for profit; he therefore memorialized to have him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissioner Tuohuan was deeply corrupt; he memorialized for his dismissal and secured it.

sentences.zh: 群盜歐南喜僭王號，偽署丞相、招討，衆號十萬。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Ou Nanxi usurped a royal title, falsely appointed chancellors and pacification commissioners, and his followers were said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Ou Nanxi declared himself king, set up a false government with chancellors and pacification commissioners, and claimed a following of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 因圖上其山川形勢，及攻取之策三十餘條，遂與都元帥課兒伯海牙、宣慰都元帥白佐、萬戶王守信等，分兵搤之。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted maps of the mountains and rivers and terrain, together with more than thirty plans for attack and capture. Then with the commander-in-chief Kuo'erbo Haiya, pacification commander-in-chief Bai Zuo, commander of ten thousand households Wang Shouxin, and others, he divided forces to block them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted maps of the terrain and more than thirty plans of attack, then joined the commander-in-chief Kuo'erbo Haiya, pacification commander-in-chief Bai Zuo, and the commander Wang Shouxin in dividing forces to hem the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 未幾，右丞唆都督兵征占城、交阯，屬護餉道。

translations.literal: Before long the right chancellor So supervised troops in the campaign against Champa and Jiaozhi, and Helapuhua was placed in charge of protecting the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the right chancellor So led troops against Champa and Jiaozhi, and Helapuhua was assigned to guard the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 比至東莞、博羅二界中，遇劇賊歐、鍾等，橫絕石灣，其鋒銳甚。

translations.literal: When he reached the border between Dongguan and Boluo he encountered the fierce bandits Ou, Zhong, and others, who barred Shawan crossing; their momentum was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Between Dongguan and Boluo he met the fierce bandits Ou, Zhong, and others blocking Shawan crossing with a very sharp attack.

sentences.zh: 合剌普華身先士卒，且戰且行，矢竭馬創，徒步格鬪，殺數十人，勇氣益厲，以衆寡不敵，為所執。

translations.literal: Helapuhua took the lead before his soldiers, fighting as he advanced. When his arrows were spent and his horse wounded, he fought on foot, killed several tens of men, and his courage grew fiercer still. Because his numbers were too few to match the enemy, he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Helapuhua led from the front, fighting as he advanced. When his arrows were gone and his horse wounded, he fought on foot, killed dozens of men, and fought all the fiercer until, outnumbered, he was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊欲奉之為主，不屈，遂遇害于中心岡。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to make him their leader; he would not yield and was therefore killed at Center Hill.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits wanted to make him their leader; he refused and was killed at Center Hill.

sentences.zh: 是夕，其妻希台特勒氏，夢其來告曰：「吾死矣。

translations.literal: That evening his wife, Lady Xitaitiele, dreamed that he came to tell her: "I am dead."
translations.idiomatic: That night his wife Lady Xitaitiele dreamed that he came to her and said: "I am dead."

sentences.zh: 」知事張德、劉閏亦夢之，二人相繼死。

translations.literal: The clerks Zhang De and Liu Run also dreamed of him; the two died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks Zhang De and Liu Run dreamed of him as well; both died soon after.

sentences.zh: 而軍中往往見其乘騅督戰云。

translations.literal: In the army many often saw him riding a piebald horse to direct the battle, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers in the army often said they saw him riding a piebald horse and directing the fighting.

sentences.zh: 後贈戶部尚書、守忠全節功臣，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue and the title of Merit Subject Who Preserves Loyalty and Integrity in Full; his posthumous name was Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously made Minister of Revenue and Merit Subject Who Preserves Loyalty and Integrity in Full, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 子二人：偰文質，越倫質。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Qiwenzhi and Yuelunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons were Qiwenzhi and Yuelunzhi.

sentences.zh: 偰文質官至吉安路達魯花赤，贈宣惠安遠功臣、禮部尚書，追封雲中郡侯，謚忠襄。

translations.literal: Qiwenzhi reached the office of darughachi of Ji'an Circuit; posthumously he was granted the title of Merit Subject Who Proclaims Grace and Pacifies the Distant, Minister of Rites, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yunzhong Commandery, with posthumous name Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwenzhi rose to darughachi of Ji'an Circuit and was posthumously made Merit Subject Who Proclaims Grace and Pacifies the Distant, Minister of Rites, and Marquis of Yunzhong Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 子六人，偰玉立、偰直堅、偰哲篤、偰朝吾、偰列箎，皆第進士。

translations.literal: He had six sons—Qiyuli, Qizhijian, Qizhedu, Qichaowu, and Qiliechi—all of whom passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Six sons—Qiyuli, Qizhijian, Qizhedu, Qichaowu, and Qiliechi—each earned the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 偰哲篤官至江西行省右丞，以文學政事稱于時。

translations.literal: Qizhedu reached the office of right chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was renowned in his time for literary learning and administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhedu rose to right chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was famed in his day for scholarship and governance.

sentences.zh: 越倫質子善著，偰哲篤子偰百僚遜，善著子正宗、阿兒思蘭，皆相繼登第。

translations.literal: Yuelunzhi's son Shanzhe, Qizhedu's son Qibailiaoxun, and Shanzhe's sons Zhengzong and A'ersilan all passed the examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhe son of Yuelunzhi, Qibailiaoxun son of Qizhedu, and Zhengzong and A'ersilan sons of Shanzhe all took the examinations and passed in turn.

sentences.zh: 一門世科之盛，當時所希有，君子蓋以為其忠義之報云。

translations.literal: The splendor of successive examination successes in one household was rare in that age; gentlemen generally regarded it as the reward of his loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Such a run of examination successes in one family was rare in that age; men of discernment took it as the reward of his loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 劉天孚字裕民，大名人。

translations.literal: Liu Tianfu, courtesy name Yumin, was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tianfu, courtesy name Yumin, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 由中書譯史為東平緫管府判官，改都漕運司判官，知冠州，再知許州，所至有治績。

translations.literal: From a translation clerk in the Secretariat he became assistant administrator of the Dongping Chief Administrator's office, then assistant administrator of the Chief Transport Office, prefect of Guanzhou, and again prefect of Xuzhou; wherever he went he had achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a translation clerk in the Secretariat, he became assistant administrator of the Dongping Chief Administrator's office, then of the Chief Transport Office, and served as prefect of Guanzhou and then Xuzhou, winning a record of good governance everywhere he went.

sentences.zh: 時檢核屯田，臨潁鄧艾口民稻田三百頃，有欲害之者，指為古屯，陳于中書，請復築之。

translations.literal: At that time garrison fields were being inspected. At Deng'ai Ford in Linying, three hundred qing of the people's rice fields—some who wished to harm them pointed to them as ancient garrison land and reported to the Secretariat, requesting that they be restored and fortified.
translations.idiomatic: During an inspection of garrison lands, enemies of the people at Deng'ai Ford in Linying claimed three hundred qing of their rice fields as ancient garrison land and petitioned the Secretariat to seize and fortify them.

sentences.zh: 中書下天孚按實，天孚為辨其非，章數上，乃止。

translations.literal: The Secretariat sent the matter down to Tianfu for investigation. Tianfu argued on their behalf that it was not so, submitted several memorials, and only then was it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat ordered Tianfu to investigate. He showed the claim was false and submitted several memorials until the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 襄城與葉縣接壤，其南為湛河，襄城民食滄鹽，葉縣民食解鹽，刻石河南岸以為界。

translations.literal: Xiangcheng bordered Yexian; to the south was the Zhan River. The people of Xiangcheng ate Cang salt, the people of Yexian ate Jie salt, and stones were carved on the south bank of the river to mark the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangcheng bordered Yexian, with the Zhan River to the south. Xiangcheng people used Cang salt and Yexian people used Jie salt; boundary stones were set on the south bank of the river.

sentences.zh: 葉縣令有貪污者，妄徙石於北二里，誣其民食私鹽，繫治百餘家。

translations.literal: A corrupt magistrate of Yexian falsely moved the stone two li to the north, accused its people of eating illicit salt, and imprisoned and prosecuted more than a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt magistrate of Yexian moved the boundary stone two li north, accused the people of using illicit salt, and prosecuted more than a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 兩縣鬪辯，葉縣倚陝漕勢以凌襄城。

translations.literal: The two counties quarreled in dispute; Yexian relied on the power of the Shaanxi transport office to bully Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The two counties quarreled, and Yexian used the power of the Shaanxi transport office to bully Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 中書遣官察其實，天孚為考其元界，移石故處，而葉縣令被罪去。

translations.literal: The Secretariat sent an official to investigate the facts. Tianfu examined the original boundary, moved the stone back to its former place, and the magistrate of Yexian was punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat sent an investigator; Tianfu traced the original boundary, restored the stone, and the Yexian magistrate was punished and removed.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，天孚禱即雨。

translations.literal: In a year of great drought Tianfu prayed and rain fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe drought he prayed and rain fell at once.

sentences.zh: 野有蝗，天孚令民出捕，俄群烏來，啄蝗為盡。

translations.literal: Locusts appeared in the fields; Tianfu ordered the people to go out and catch them. Soon flocks of birds came and pecked the locusts until none remained.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts appeared in the fields he ordered the people to hunt them; soon flocks of birds came and devoured the locusts completely.

sentences.zh: 明年麥熟時，有青蟲如蟊，食麥，人無可奈何，忽生大華蟲，盡嚼之。

translations.literal: The next year when the wheat ripened, green insects like locusts ate the wheat and people could do nothing about it. Suddenly large patterned insects appeared and devoured them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the wheat ripened, green locust-like insects devoured the crop and nothing could be done—until large patterned insects suddenly appeared and ate them all.

sentences.zh: 許人立碑頌焉。

translations.literal: The people of Xu erected a stele in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xu erected a stele in his praise.

sentences.zh: 轉萬億寶源庫同提舉，遷江西行省左右司郎中，以母老不赴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to associate intendant of the Treasury of Myriad Millions and Precious Sources, then promoted to director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, but because his mother was old he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to associate intendant of the Treasury of Myriad Millions and Precious Sources and promoted to director in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, but declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was in mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起知河中府，視事始兩月，陝西行省丞相阿思罕為亂，舉兵至河中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to serve as prefect of Hezhong Prefecture. He had been in office only two months when Ashihan, chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, rebelled and led troops to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled as prefect of Hezhong. He had been in office only two months when Ashihan, chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, rebelled and marched on the city.

sentences.zh: 時事起不虞，達魯花赤朶兒只趨晉寧告亂，天孚日夜治戰守具，選丁壯，分守要害。

translations.literal: The affair arose unexpectedly. The darughachi Duo'erzhi hurried to Jining to report the rebellion. Tianfu day and night prepared weapons for war and defense, selected able-bodied men, and assigned them to guard critical points.
translations.idiomatic: The revolt came without warning. The darughachi Duo'erzhi rode to Jining to report it while Tianfu worked night and day on arms and defenses, chose able-bodied men, and posted them at the critical points.

sentences.zh: 令河東縣達魯花赤脫因都守大慶關津口，盡收船舫東岸。

translations.literal: He ordered the Hedong County darughachi Tuoyindu to hold the Daqing Pass crossing and gather all boats to the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Hedong County darughachi Tuoyindu to hold the Daqing Pass crossing and pull every boat to the east bank.

sentences.zh: 令判官孫伯帖木兒守汾陰，推官程謙守禹門，河東縣尹王文義守風陵等渡。

translations.literal: He ordered the assistant administrator Sunbotiemuer to hold Fenyin, the investigating officer Cheng Qian to hold Yumen, and the Hedong County magistrate Wang Weny to hold the crossings at Fengling and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He posted the assistant administrator Sunbotiemuer at Fenyin, the investigating officer Cheng Qian at Yumen, and the Hedong County magistrate Wang Weny at the Fengling crossings.

sentences.zh: 阿思罕軍列柵河西岸，使來索舟，天孚度不能拒，凡八遣人至晉寧乞援兵，不報。

translations.literal: Ashihan's army set palisades on the west bank of the river and sent men to demand boats. Tianfu judged that he could not refuse; eight times he sent men to Jining to beg for relief troops, but no answer came.
translations.idiomatic: Ashihan's army camped on the west bank and demanded boats. Tianfu knew he could not hold them off; eight times he sent to Jining for reinforcements, but none came.

sentences.zh: 居七日，阿思罕縛筏河上，欲縱火屠城，同知府事鐵哥，與河東廉訪副使明安荅見事急，且患城中人偪，乃詣阿思罕軍，阿思罕囚之，而斂船濟兵。

translations.literal: After seven days Ashihan bound rafts on the river and intended to set fire and slaughter the city. The co-prefect Tiege and the Hedong surveillance vice-commissioner Ming'anda, seeing the affair urgent and also fearing pressure from the people in the city, therefore went to Ashihan's army. Ashihan imprisoned them and gathered boats to ferry troops across.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days Ashihan lashed rafts on the river, intending to burn the city and slaughter its people. The co-prefect Tiege and the Hedong surveillance vice-commissioner Ming'anda, seeing the crisis and fearing pressure from the townspeople, went to Ashihan's camp. He imprisoned them and gathered boats to ferry his troops across.

sentences.zh: 兵既入城，阿思罕以扼河渡、鎖舟楫為天孚罪，欲脅使附己。
