translations.literal: Once the troops had entered the city, Ashihan charged Tianfu with blocking the river crossing and locking up the boats, wishing to coerce him to join his side.
translations.idiomatic: Once his troops were in the city, Ashihan blamed Tianfu for blocking the crossing and seizing the boats and tried to force him to join the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 方坐府治，號令諸軍，天孚佩刀直前，衆遏之，不得進。

translations.literal: Just as he sat in the prefectural hall issuing orders to the armies, Tianfu, wearing his sword, went straight forward. The crowd blocked him and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: As Ashihan sat in the prefectural hall giving orders, Tianfu drew his sword and strode forward, but the crowd blocked him and he could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 退謂幕僚王從善等曰：「吾家本微賤，荷朝命至此，今不幸遭大變，吾何忍從之，而負上恩哉！

translations.literal: He withdrew and said to his staff officer Wang Congshan and others: "My family was originally humble and lowly; we received the court's command to reach this post. Now, having unhappily met this great calamity, how could I bear to follow him and fail the sovereign's grace!"
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and told his staff officer Wang Congshan and the others: "My family was humble; the court raised me to this post. Now that disaster has struck, how can I join him and betray the emperor's grace!"

sentences.zh: 且與其辱於阿思罕之手，吾寧蹈河以死。

translations.literal: Rather than suffer disgrace at Ashihan's hands, I would rather tread the river and die.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather throw myself into the river than suffer dishonor at Ashihan's hands.

sentences.zh: 」遂拂衣出。

translations.literal: He then shook out his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shook out his robes and left.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，河冰方堅，天孚拔所佩刀斫冰開，北望為國語若祝謝者，再拜已，脫衣帽岸滸，乃投水中。

translations.literal: The weather was cold and the river ice had just hardened. Tianfu drew the sword at his belt and hacked the ice open. Looking north he spoke in the state language as if in prayer and thanksgiving, bowed twice, removed his hat and robe on the bank, and cast himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitter cold and the river had frozen hard. Tianfu drew his sword, hacked through the ice, looked north and spoke in Mongol as though in prayer, bowed twice, set down his hat and robe on the bank, and threw himself into the water.

sentences.zh: 阿思罕大怒，籍其家。

translations.literal: Ashihan was greatly enraged and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: Ashihan was furious and confiscated his family's property.

sentences.zh: 郡人咸哀痛之。

translations.literal: All the people of the prefecture mourned him in grief.
translations.idiomatic: The whole prefecture mourned him in grief.

sentences.zh: 事平，詔其弟天惠，給驛以歸其柩，葬于大名。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an edict ordered his younger brother Tianhui to be given post-horses to bring back his coffin, and he was buried at Daming.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, the court ordered his younger brother Tianhui to use post-horses to bring back his coffin, and he was buried at Daming.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠秉節功臣、中奉大夫、河東山西道宣慰使、護軍、彭城郡侯，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Merit Subject Who Pushes Sincerity and Upholds Integrity, Palace Attendant, pacification commissioner of the Hedong-Shanxi Circuit, protector of the army, and Marquis of Pengcheng Commandery, with posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Merit Subject Who Pushes Sincerity and Upholds Integrity, Palace Attendant, pacification commissioner of the Hedong-Shanxi Circuit, protector of the army, and Marquis of Pengcheng Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 蕭景茂，漳州龍溪人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Jingmao was a man of Longxi in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingmao came from Longxi in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性剛直孝友。

translations.literal: His nature was upright, firm, filial, and friendly to his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright, steadfast, filial, and devoted to his kin.

sentences.zh: 家貧力農。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he labored at farming.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and he worked the fields.

sentences.zh: 重改至元四年，南勝縣民李智甫作亂，掠龍溪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era, Li Zhifu of Nansheng County rebelled and plundered Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era, Li Zhifu of Nansheng County rebelled and raided Longxi.

sentences.zh: 景茂與兄佑集鄉丁拒之，據觀音山橋險，與賊戰。

translations.literal: Jingmao and his elder brother You gathered village militia to resist them, held the defensible ground at Guanyin Mountain Bridge, and fought the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao and his elder brother You rallied village militia, held Guanyin Mountain Bridge, and fought the rebels.

sentences.zh: 衆敗，景茂被執。

translations.literal: The force was defeated and Jingmao was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Their force was defeated and Jingmao was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 賊脅使從己，景茂罵曰：「狗盜！

translations.literal: The bandits coerced him to follow them. Jingmao reviled them, saying: "Dog-thieves!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to force him to join them. Jingmao cursed them: "Dog-thieves!"

sentences.zh: 我生為大元民，死作隔洲鬼，豈從汝為逆耶！

translations.literal: "Born I am a subject of the Great Yuan; dead I shall be a ghost of Gezhou—how could I follow you in rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: "Alive I am a man of the Great Yuan; dead I shall haunt Gezhou—never will I follow you in treason!"

sentences.zh: 」隔洲，其所居里也。

translations.literal: Gezhou was the village where he dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Gezhou was the name of his home village.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，縛景茂於樹，臠其肉，使自啖。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged, bound Jingmao to a tree, sliced his flesh, and made him eat it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels bound him to a tree, cut slices from his flesh, and forced him to eat them.

sentences.zh: 景茂益憤罵，賊遂以刀決其口，至耳傍，景茂罵不絕聲而死。

translations.literal: Jingmao cursed all the more in fury. The bandits then used a knife to cut open his mouth as far as beside his ear. Jingmao cursed without cease until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao only cursed the louder. The rebels slashed his mouth open with a knife to the ear, but he never stopped cursing until he died.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事，朝廷命褒表之，仍給錢以葬。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported the matter upward. The court ordered that he be praised and commemorated, and also provided money for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the affair to the court, which ordered him honored and commemorated and provided funds for his burial.
